title: DBSCAN
subtitle: Density-Based Spatial Clustering & Noise Detection
summary: Discover arbitrarily shaped clusters via ε-neighborhood density while isolating noise outliers.

evaluationChart.title: Sorted K-Distance Reachability Plot
evaluationChart.description: Sharp upward knee in the k-distance curve reveals the optimal ε radius separating dense clusters from noise.

advantages: Does not require specifying the number of clusters K upfront.
Discovers arbitrary non-convex shapes (rings, crescents, bands).
Explicitly flags low-density outliers as Noise (-1) instead of forcing them into clusters.
limitations: Struggles when clusters have widely varying densities.
Sensitive to ε and minPts hyperparameter selection.
Distance metrics degrade in very high dimensions.

formulas.label: ε-Neighborhood
formulas.description: Points within radius epsilon of point p.

formulas.label: Core Point Condition
formulas.description: A point is Core if its ε-neighborhood contains at least minPts points.

hyperparameters.label: Epsilon Radius (ε)
hyperparameters.description: Neighborhood search radius around each point.

hyperparameters.label: Min Points (minPts)
hyperparameters.description: Minimum neighbors required to form a dense Core point.

codeTemplates.fromScratch:
import numpy as np

def region_query(X, idx, eps):
    return np.where(np.linalg.norm(X - X[idx], axis=1) <= eps)[0]

# Core points satisfy len(region_query) >= min_pts
codeTemplates.scikitLearn:
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1.8,2.2],[2.2,2.6],[2.5,2.0],[6.4,6.2],[6.9,6.7],[8.6,1.8]])
labels = DBSCAN(eps=1.1, min_samples=3).fit_predict(X)
print('Cluster labels (-1 = noise):', labels)
